title: The subcategory Rep_Φ(G)
body_html:
The subcategory $\Rep_\Phi(G)$

For a compatible system $\Phi = (\mathscr{K}_+, \phi)$ (see [[node:coefficient_systems.semisimple_character_T_axioms]]):

Definition. $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is the full subcategory of $\Rep(G)$ on those $V$ such that $V$ is generated, as a $G$-module, by $\bigcup_{x \in [\![A]\!]_0} V[\phi_x]$, with $x$ ranging over the vertices of the apartment $A$.

Equivalence with summing over all vertices of $\BSigma$. By $G$-equivariance (T3), $V[\phi_{gx}] = g \cdot V[\phi_x]$ for $g \in G$; since $G \cdot A = \BSigma$ (every facet of $\BSigma$ is a $G$-translate of a facet of $A$), the $G$-submodule generated by $\bigcup_{x \in [\![A]\!]_0} V[\phi_x]$ equals the one generated by $\bigcup_{y \in [\![\BSigma]\!]_0} V[\phi_y]$. Both formulations give the same $\Rep_\Phi(G)$.

This is the higher-depth analogue of The subcategory Rep_φ(G); indeed, when $\Phi$ comes from depth-zero data $(G_{\bullet,0+}, \mathbf 1)$ on the ordinary building $\mathcal{B}(G)$, $\Rep_\Phi(G) = \Rep_0(G)$.

For the resolution theorem Resolution theorem: C_•(Φ, V) → V (Thm 7.1.7) and the localization equivalence Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ)[E_Φ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_Φ(G) (§7.4 Thm) one assumes:

Hypothesis (S). $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ is a Serre subcategory of $\Rep(G)$.

(S) is verified for classical groups via [HKSS, Prop 6.7] and for tame types via the Bernstein decomposition + [KY, Thm 6.3] — see Hypothesis (S) for classical groups via [HKSS] and Hypothesis (S) for tame types via Bernstein + [KY].
